neighbours.label: existential ' there' before 'was/were' in scriptural or old-chronicle narration ('In those days there was no king'); the subject slot just before a copula in archaic prose; quiet on modern reporting
fire: And in that land there was a famine, and the people were sore afraid.
It is written in the ancient annals that there was a prince who ruled seven cities.
Now there was a man of the hill country whose name was Elkanah.
In the days of the judges there was a drought upon all the earth.
And it came to pass that there was a great storm upon the sea.
The old scribes relate that there were giants in the north in those times.
And there was war between the two houses all their days.
In the reign of that king there was peace throughout the realm.
quiet: The farm report says the harvest was poor and prices rose sharply.
The guidebook mentions a prince who ruled seven cities long ago.
A man from the hill country named Elkanah owned the shop.
The drought of last summer damaged crops across the region.
A great storm hit the coast and sank several fishing boats.
The police said there were two witnesses in the lobby.
The two families fought in court for most of the decade.
The manager confirmed there was a delay at the warehouse.
